# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run mcp:tools-doc`. Do not edit by hand: this file is
     produced from a live `tools/list` response so it cannot drift. -->

Server `upgradr-mcp-worker` version `0.1.0`, protocol `2025-06-18`, 16 tools, 3 prompts.

See [mcp.md](./mcp.md) for authorization, scopes, and how to connect. Every tool below is additionally gated by the `mcp` scope and by row-level security, so a tool only ever sees the calling user's own data.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | Allows this client to reach your workspace at all. Required. |
| `profile:read` | Your confirmed experience, education, skills, and job search preferences. Unreviewed imports are never shared. |
| `opportunities:read` | Lets the agent see which opportunities you already track so it does not propose the same job twice. |
| `applications:read` | Your opportunities, statuses, follow-ups, notes, and document titles. |
| `applications:write` | Create job proposals in your Inbox, move cards between columns, and add follow-ups and notes. |
| `applications:delete` | Permanently remove items. Every deletion still requires a separate confirmation step. |

## Prompts

Named workflows that sequence the tools above. A client surfaces them as slash commands or menu entries, so a user can invoke one by name instead of describing the steps. Prompt text is generated from the caller's granted scopes, so the wording below reflects a full-scope grant.

| Prompt | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `weekly_job_search` | `focus`?, `maxProposals`? | Find new openings that fit the user's profile and add them to their Inbox as proposals, without re-proposing anything they already track or previously closed. |
| `review_pipeline` | `horizon`? | Walk the user's active pipeline and report what needs attention: overdue follow-ups, stalled opportunities, and the next concrete actions. |
| `triage_proposals` | _none_ | Go through the opportunities waiting in the Inbox and recommend, with reasoning, which to shortlist and which to close. |

## get_candidate_profile

**Get candidate profile**

Return the user's confirmed candidate profile: headline, summary, relevant experience, work experience, education, and skills. This is EVIDENCE, not intent. Use it to judge whether a role you have already found is a good fit, and to write `matchScore` and `matchRationale` grounded in specific experience, education, or skills rather than in generalities. `relevantExperience` is free-text background (often the user's whole CV) and is usually the richest source here, so read it before falling back on the structured lists, which many users leave empty rather than re-keying data they already have in a CV. An empty `experiences`/`education`/`skills` therefore means 'not entered', never 'no such background'. Do not use it to decide what to search for -- that is `get_job_search_preferences`, and the two routinely differ: a user whose profile reads 'Senior iOS Engineer' may be deliberately looking for engineering management. Where they conflict, the preferences win, because they are what the user wants next rather than what they have done. Unconfirmed or imported-but-unreviewed facts are never returned, so treat everything here as user-confirmed.

Requires scope: `profile:read` (plus `mcp`).

_No arguments._

Returns:

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headline` | string \| null | yes | How the user describes their current position. |
| `summary` | string \| null | yes | Career narrative in the user's own words. |
| `relevantExperience` | string \| null | yes | Free-text background evidence: roles, projects, technologies, and dates, either written by the user or extracted from their CV. Usually the richest source for judging fit — quote from it in matchRationale. It is evidence about the candidate, never a search filter. |
| `lastReviewedAt` | string \| null | yes | When the user last confirmed this profile is current. |
| `experiences` | array of object | yes | Confirmed employment history, most relevant first. Cite it in matchRationale. |
| `experiences[].company` | string | yes |  |
| `experiences[].title` | string | yes |  |
| `experiences[].description` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `experiences[].startDate` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `experiences[].endDate` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `experiences[].isCurrent` | boolean | yes |  |
| `education` | array of object | yes | Confirmed education and certifications. |
| `education[].institution` | string | yes |  |
| `education[].degree` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `education[].fieldOfStudy` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `skills` | array of object | yes | Confirmed skills. `evidence` is the user's own justification, not an inference. |
| `skills[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `skills[].evidence` | string \| null | yes |  |

## get_job_search_preferences

**Get job search preferences**

Return the user's search brief. This is INTENT: use it to build your queries and to reject candidates before they ever reach the user. `get_candidate_profile` is the separate rubric you score a surviving candidate against. HARD constraints -- a candidate failing one of these must not be proposed: - `excludedCompanies`: never propose these employers, under any circumstances. - `locations` together with `remotePolicy`: a role the user cannot take is not a candidate. A remote role the user can do from a listed location satisfies this even when the company sits elsewhere. - `minimumCompensation`: see the rules below, which matter because most postings state no pay at all. - `industries`, when non-empty: stay inside them. Sector labels are a judgement call, so say which you assigned when it was not obvious. DIRECTIONAL, not hard: - `targetRoles`: the shape of what the user wants, not an allow-list of titles. A strong adjacent role is worth proposing -- say why in `matchRationale`. - `notes`: free text the user wrote for you about constraints and dealbreakers. Read it before searching; it can add hard constraints the structured fields cannot express. COMPENSATION. `minimumCompensation` is a gross pre-tax floor in `compensationCurrency`, quoted per `minimumCompensationPeriod`. Normalize a posting's figure into that period before comparing -- an annual figure tested against a monthly floor is wrong by a factor of 12. Compare against the BOTTOM of an advertised range. A posting that states no compensation is NOT a failed test: most do not state one. Propose it and say the pay was unstated. If the posting is in another currency, this app has no exchange-rate source, so convert it yourself and state the rate you used in `matchRationale`. Check `isConfigured` first. When it is false the user has never set a brief, and searching on this empty row would produce an unconstrained search they never asked for.

Requires scope: `profile:read` (plus `mcp`).

_No arguments._

Returns:

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `targetRoles` | array of string | yes | The kinds of role the user wants next. DIRECTIONAL, not an allow-list: a strong adjacent role is worth proposing if you justify it. |
| `locations` | array of string | yes | Where the user can work. Hard constraint, read together with remotePolicy. |
| `remotePolicy` | `onsite` \| `hybrid` \| `remote` \| `flexible` | yes | How the user will work. A remote role they can do from a listed location satisfies the location constraint even when the employer sits elsewhere. |
| `minimumCompensation` | number \| null | yes | Gross pre-tax floor, in compensationCurrency and per minimumCompensationPeriod. Hard constraint, but a posting that states no pay has NOT failed it -- propose it and flag the pay as unstated. |
| `minimumCompensationPeriod` | `month` \| `year` | yes | The period minimumCompensation is quoted in. Normalize a posting's figure into this period before comparing: an annual figure tested against a monthly floor is wrong by a factor of 12. |
| `compensationCurrency` | string \| null | yes | ISO 4217 code for the floor. This app has no exchange-rate source, so converting a posting quoted in another currency is your job -- state the rate you used. |
| `industries` | array of string | yes | Hard constraint when non-empty. Say which sector you assigned when it is arguable. |
| `excludedCompanies` | array of string | yes | Never propose these employers, under any circumstances. |
| `notes` | string \| null | yes | Free text the user wrote for you. May add hard constraints the structured fields cannot express, so read it before searching. |
| `isConfigured` | boolean | yes | False when the user has never set a brief. Every account is seeded with an empty preferences row at signup, so without this flag an unconfigured row is indistinguishable from a deliberately wide-open search. When false, do not search on the empty row: infer a brief from the candidate profile and state in your report that you did so and what you assumed. |
| `updatedAt` | string \| null | yes | When the user last saved these filters. Stale filters are still their stated intent -- mention the age rather than overriding them. |

## search_existing_opportunities

**Search existing opportunities**

Search the user's already-tracked applications by title/company/location/source URL, to check for an existing match before proposing a new one.

Requires scope: `opportunities:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | no | Match against the job title. Partial matches count. |
| `companyName` | string | no | Match against the company name. Partial matches count. |
| `location` | string | no | Narrow results by location. Only meaningful alongside another filter. |
| `sourceUrl` | string | no | Exact posting URL. The most precise way to check whether a job is already tracked. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum results, 1-50. Defaults to a bounded page. |

## list_known_opportunity_keys

**List known opportunity keys**

Return the de-duplication keys for every opportunity the user already tracks, including closed ones, so an agent can filter its candidates locally before calling create_job_proposals. Each entry carries the canonical source URL, the source provider and its external job id, a normalized company|title|location fingerprint, and the current status. An entry with isClosed true means the user already rejected, withdrew from, dismissed, or archived that opportunity: do not propose it again. The suppressions list carries rules the user set explicitly -- a muted company, a muted role, or a posting they closed -- and applies even to opportunities whose row has since been deleted. Never propose anything matching one; create_job_proposals will refuse it. Fetch this once per run (paginate with offset, or pass updatedSince to fetch only what changed) rather than searching per candidate.

Requires scope: `opportunities:read` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `updatedSince` | string | no | ISO 8601 timestamp. Return only keys for opportunities changed since then, so a repeat run can fetch just the delta. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Keys per page, 1-200. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Number of keys to skip, for paging. |

## create_job_proposals

**Create job proposals**

Propose up to 20 new job opportunities for the user to review. Each proposal must cite a valid HTTP(S) source URL. Duplicates are detected server-side against every opportunity the user owns, including ones they already closed, so no proposal is ever silently duplicated: each item comes back as created, duplicate (same provider job id or same canonical source URL), or possible_duplicate (same company, title and location found at a different URL). An item may also come back as suppressed, meaning the user has asked never to see it again -- a muted company or role, or a posting they closed. That is a decision only the user can reverse, so do not retry it and do not work around it with a different URL. Duplicate results include the existing opportunity's id and current status, so a closed match means the user already rejected or dismissed that job — do not propose it again. Set allowSimilar on an item only to override a possible_duplicate you have confirmed is a genuinely different opening. Use list_known_opportunity_keys once per run to filter candidates before calling this tool.

Requires scope: `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proposals` | array of object | yes | Between 1 and 20 proposals, each evaluated independently. |
| `proposals[].title` | string | yes | Job title exactly as published, e.g. 'Senior iOS Engineer'. |
| `proposals[].companyName` | string | yes | Hiring company name. Used for duplicate detection, so keep it consistent. |
| `proposals[].location` | string | no | Work location as published, e.g. 'Stockholm, Sweden' or 'Remote (EU)'. |
| `proposals[].sourceUrl` | string | yes | Canonical HTTP(S) URL of the posting. Required, and the strongest duplicate key. |
| `proposals[].sourceProvider` | string | yes | Where it was found, e.g. 'linkedin', 'greenhouse', 'company-site'. |
| `proposals[].externalId` | string | no | The provider's own stable job id, when the posting exposes one. Supply it whenever available: combined with sourceProvider it is the most reliable duplicate key, and it survives URL changes. |
| `proposals[].description` | string | no | Job description text. Stored verbatim for the user to read. |
| `proposals[].compensationMin` | number | no | Bottom of the published salary range, exactly as the posting states it. Do not convert to another period -- send compensationPeriod alongside and the app normalizes when comparing against the user's floor. |
| `proposals[].compensationMax` | number | no | Top of the published salary range, in the same period and currency as compensationMin. |
| `proposals[].compensationPeriod` | `month` \| `year` | no | Whether the range above is per 'month' or per 'year'. Required whenever you send an amount. State what the posting said rather than converting; if it quotes an hourly or daily rate, convert to a monthly figure yourself and say so in matchRationale, since that conversion needs an assumption about hours worked that only you can make. |
| `proposals[].compensationCurrency` | string | no | ISO 4217 currency code for the compensation range, e.g. 'SEK', 'EUR'. |
| `proposals[].matchScore` | integer | no | Your assessment of fit against the user's profile, 0-100. |
| `proposals[].matchRationale` | string | no | Short explanation of the score, shown to the user alongside the proposal. |
| `proposals[].strengths` | array of string | no | Concrete reasons the user fits this role. |
| `proposals[].gaps` | array of string | no | Requirements the user does not clearly meet. Be honest; this is decision support. |
| `proposals[].confidence` | number | no | How confident you are in the extracted facts themselves, 0-1. |
| `proposals[].allowSimilar` | boolean | no | Override a possible_duplicate result for this item only, when you have confirmed it is a genuinely different opening. Exact source-URL and provider job-id duplicates can never be overridden. |

## assess_job_match

**Assess job match**

Record a match assessment against an opportunity that already exists, for example after learning more about the role or after the user updated their profile. Each call appends a new, attributed entry to the opportunity's assessment history and becomes its current score; earlier assessments are kept so the user can see how a judgement changed. Supply at least a score or a rationale. strengths and gaps replace the previous lists rather than adding to them. To propose an opportunity the user does not have yet, use create_job_proposals instead — this tool never creates one.

Requires scopes: `applications:read`, `applications:write` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Id of the opportunity to assess, as returned by search_applications. |
| `matchScore` | integer | no | Your assessment of fit against the user's profile, 0-100. |
| `matchRationale` | string | no | Short explanation of the score, shown to the user alongside the opportunity. |
| `strengths` | array of string | no | Concrete reasons the user fits this role. Replaces the previous list. |
| `gaps` | array of string | no | Requirements the user does not clearly meet. Replaces the previous list. |
| `confidence` | number | no | How confident you are in the extracted facts themselves, 0-1. |

**Move application status**

| `note` | string | no | Why the status changed. Shown to the user on the activity timeline. |

## prepare_destructive_operation

**Prepare destructive operation**

Request a single-use confirmation token for a destructive action (e.g. deleting an application, follow-up, or note, or archiving a batch of applications). The action does not happen until confirm_operation is called with the returned token, and the token expires after 15 minutes.

Requires scope: `applications:delete` (plus `mcp`).

One of the following shapes:

**operationType: `delete_application`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_application` | yes |  |
| `applicationId` | string | yes | Opportunity to delete, along with its notes, follow-ups, and history. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `delete_follow_up`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_follow_up` | yes |  |
| `followUpId` | string | yes | Follow-up task to delete. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `delete_note`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `delete_note` | yes |  |
| `noteId` | string | yes | Note to delete. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

**operationType: `bulk_archive_applications`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationType` | `bulk_archive_applications` | yes |  |
| `applicationIds` | array of string | yes | Between 1 and 20 opportunities to archive in a single confirmed operation. |
| `reason` | string | no | Why this is being deleted. Shown to the user in the confirmation summary and kept in the audit trail. |

## confirm_operation

**Confirm operation**

Execute a previously prepared destructive operation using its single-use confirmation token from prepare_destructive_operation.

Requires scope: `applications:delete` (plus `mcp`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operationToken` | string | yes | The single-use token returned by prepare_destructive_operation. Valid for 15 minutes, and only for the exact operation that was summarized. |

## Calling a tool

```sh
curl -sS "$UPGRADR_MCP_URL" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $UPGRADR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_job_search_dashboard","arguments":{}}}'
```

Get `$UPGRADR_ACCESS_TOKEN` from `npm run mcp:login -- --email you@example.com`.
